investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-29T21:44–21:52Z because every pod submitted to the production Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes and the other 4 nodes were excluded by node affinity/selector rules. Because no pod reached a running state, the createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'], neither of which can be satisfied without a running pod.
source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: all three remote-agent checks share the same swarm-backed VM provisioning path, explaining the uniform failure across all siblings.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the cluster has no remaining VM slots to schedule new remote-agent pods, and preemption found no victims to evict (evidenced by failed-check.message and both sibling messages).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes are permanently excluded from remote-agent scheduling, concentrating all capacity pressure on only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., leaked VMs, node resize, or quota reduction), all remote-agent evals fail simultaneously.

Tertiary — VM resource leak from a prior eval run: if a previous remote-agent eval did not clean up its VM (e.g., withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs failed), the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on those 2 nodes may still be held, preventing new allocations.
Lower confidence — quota or limit change on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource at the namespace or node level that reduced available slots below the concurrent demand of the three sibling evals.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to create a remote agent was left unschedulable — the Kubernetes scheduler reported 0/6 nodes available, with 2 nodes showing insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes failing pod node-affinity/selector matching. No required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past the createAgent call.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also attempted and found no victims. As a result, every probe attempt to create a remote agent pod timed out unscheduled (~144–150 s), preventing the eval runner from reaching the state-polling step and producing any evidence output. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-29T21:44–21:52Z because every pod submitted to the production Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes and the other 4 nodes were excluded by node affinity/selector rules. Because no pod reached a running state, the createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never completed, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 146s, latencyMs=153567.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, pod stuck for 144s, latencyMs=147255.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'], neither of which can be satisfied without a running pod.
source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: all three remote-agent checks share the same swarm-backed VM provisioning path, explaining the uniform failure across all siblings.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: the cluster has no remaining VM slots to schedule new remote-agent pods, and preemption found no victims to evict (evidenced by failed-check.message and both sibling messages).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes are permanently excluded from remote-agent scheduling, concentrating all capacity pressure on only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes lost capacity (e.g., leaked VMs, node resize, or quota reduction), all remote-agent evals fail simultaneously.

Tertiary — VM resource leak from a prior eval run: if a previous remote-agent eval did not clean up its VM (e.g., withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs failed), the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on those 2 nodes may still be held, preventing new allocations.
Lower confidence — quota or limit change on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource at the namespace or node level that reduced available slots below the concurrent demand of the three sibling evals.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to determine whether the resource is fully exhausted and whether any pods are stuck holding slots.
Identify and terminate any remote-agent pods in non-terminal states (Pending, Running but unresponsive) that may be leaking kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the eligible nodes.
Assess whether the node affinity/selector configuration intentionally restricts remote-agent pods to only 2 nodes; if so, evaluate whether additional nodes can be labeled to expand the eligible pool.
If capacity is genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, scale up kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the eligible nodes or provision additional nodes that satisfy the pod's affinity/selector.

Monitor the remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) after any remediation to confirm scheduling resumes and all 5 required evidence fields are returned.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is marked required=false in features.json (line 185), but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183–184); the required checks failing means the remote-agents feature is in a degraded/outage state per the degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 thresholds.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted (i.e., allocatable > requested), the root cause is not resource exhaustion and another scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If a subsequent eval run succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly held resource that was released) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.
If the 4 non-affinity nodes are shown to actually match the pod selector in the current cluster state, the node affinity diagnosis is incorrect and the pod spec or node labels may have diverged.
If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm on the eligible nodes at the time of re-inspection, the failure may have been caused by a temporary resource spike that has since resolved.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity directly (e.g., via the cluster API) and warns before the resource is fully exhausted, rather than only detecting exhaustion after a pod scheduling timeout.
Add an eval that verifies the count of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting if the eligible node pool shrinks unexpectedly.

Add a pre-scheduling health check eval that detects Pending pods stuck in Unschedulable state for more than a configurable threshold before the full agent lifecycle eval times out, enabling faster triage.
Consider adding a canary eval that submits a minimal remote-agent pod and checks for schedulability within a short window (e.g., 30s) to catch capacity exhaustion earlier in the eval pipeline.
